text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press at the weekend. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Romania opened its electronic over-the-counter market to trade shares derived from its mass privatisation programme.
- Cabinet pledged to monitor sunflower oil retail sales to prevent price hikes caused by intermediaries.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- U.S. Chase Manhattan Bank to loan worth $200 million to Romanian Oil Company (CRP) for crude imports.
- National Bank vice-governor Corneliu Croitoru appointed director of special fund set up to guarantee bank deposits of up to 10 million lei.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Some 15 people died in the past 48 hours due to mushroom poisoning.
- President Ion Iliescu runs for Senate on lists of ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), but he is not a PDSR member, his spokesman Traian Chebeleu said.
- Iliescu's bid for a seat in the Senate is illegal, because he is no party member, opposition politicians say.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Nicu Ceausescu's body was flown home for burial.
- Flights of state-owned airline Tarom to take off one our earlier than scheduled until October 26 due to country's shift to winter time.
ADEVARUL
- 500,000 young couples have applied for state housing.
ZIUA

- Iliescu allegedly used the popular uprising in December 1989 to organise a coup, late Nicu Ceausescu said in statement to parliament commission investigating eevnts in 1989 anti-communist revolt. ($=3,247) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
